messages:
maria: morning — seeing sharp spike in p99 latency for private eu-west-1 cluster since ~09:05 UTC. traces show TCP retries and some RSTs. Any infra changes?
sam: confirmed, CloudWatch for the NATs has a big jump in active connections and "ConnectionsDropped" metric around the same time.
maria: looked at node level: nf_conntrack_count ~124994 and nf_conntrack_max=131072. dmesg has lines: 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' and repeated 'IP tables: conntrack: table full'.
ryan: fwiw we rolled the private runtime image last night with a temporary keepalive disable (PR #428) to mitigate a socket leak reported by canary. Could be opening per-request TCPs.
lee: if keepalive=0 at runtime each request dials a new TCP session -> short-lived flows. NAT conntrack saturates quickly under high RPS and you get new dials failing or delayed, which explains observed retries/latency.
maria: commands I ran locally to confirm:
```bash
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
conntrack -S
iptables -L -v -n | grep ESTABLISHED
# and checked dmesg for 'nf_conntrack: table full'
```
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-231 - NAT conntrack saturation causing high latency in private eu-west-1 cluster. Pagerduty notified.
sam: short mitigation applied: increased net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 262144 on affected nodes and lowered `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout` from 60 -> 30, enabled `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1`. Pushed via ansible play: `ansible -i hosts -m sysctl -a "name=net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max value=262144"`
maria: also reverted the runtime keepalive change — we re-enabled keepalive=30s and turned on connection multiplexing/batching in the runtime config for private clusters. Canary at 09:45 and then widened.
ryan: profiler dump shows dramatic drop in new dials/s once keepalive restored. Before mitigation: ~3200 new dials/s on the cluster, after: ~72 new dials/s. conntrack_count fell from ~125k -> ~48k and p99 latency from ~420ms -> ~35ms.
maria: profiler snippet:
```text
09:05 dial_new: 3200/s
09:50 dial_new: 72/s
conntrack_count: 125000 -> 48000
p99_latency_ms: 420 -> 35
```
lee: follow-ups: 1) bake a permanent nf_conntrack_max bump into our private AMI defaults, 2) set runtime default keepalive=30s and ensure batching heuristics favor connection reuse, 3) add infra alert when nf_conntrack_count > 80% for >2m, 4) verify NAT gateway scaling / connection pooling for VPCs.
sam: I'll open the infra PRs and link to INC-2026-231. Also adding a dashboard tile for conntrack usage and a retro on the runtime change that disabled keepalive. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — resolved for now. Will follow up with a short postmortem once metrics stabilize and PRs land.
